verdicts.quote: If you’re building an application for others to use, we recommend you use OAuth2 authentication.
verdicts.reason: Linear publicly supports API keys and OAuth, and recommends OAuth for third‑party apps; for a multi-tenant agent toolkit OAuth2 is the primary choice.

verdicts.quote: API and webhook access — Included … API rate limits — Standard limits.
verdicts.reason: API access is included on the Free plan, and developers can create apps themselves (see “Create and manage webhooks and OAuth applications in Settings > Administration > API” in the docs), so credentials are self‑serve and available on a free tier.

verdicts.quote: In addition to querying, Linear has full support for mutating all entities.
verdicts.reason: The GraphQL API exposes core objects with full CRUD across the product, indicating broad coverage.

verdicts.quote: Linear’s MCP server follows the authenticated remote MCP spec, so the server is centrally hosted and managed… Read‑write access is provided through ‘https://mcp.linear.app/mcp’.
verdicts.reason: Linear publishes and hosts its own MCP server, so this is an official MCP.

verdicts.quote: Create and manage webhooks and OAuth applications in Settings > Administration > API.
verdicts.reason: Self‑serve OAuth and API access on the Free plan with documented webhooks and SDK/docs mean Composio could ship an integration today; no partner gating or app review is required beyond normal admin approval within a customer workspace.
